nodes.label: 26-year-old female patient presented with fever, tachypnoea, chest tightness, and vomiting
Fever and tachypnoea lasted 10 days, and chest distress worsened for 3 days before hospitalization
Patient self-treated with antipyretic painkillers; no special medical, family, or psycho-social history
Initial vital signs: temperature 37.6°C, pulse 128/min, respiratory rate 21/min, blood pressure 76/50 mmHg
ABG shows lactate 4.86 mmol/L and metabolic acidosis
NGS detects Enterococcus faecium and Klebsiella pneumoniae
Patient has septic shock with tissue hypoperfusion
Blood culture and CBC results are still pending
Sepsis caused by polymicrobial bacteremia (Enterococcus faecium and Klebsiella pneumoniae)
Sepsis secondary to pulmonary infection (Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia)
Enterococcus faecium bacteremia as the dominant bloodstream pathogen
